chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Sindi, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wasshash, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, for every Imam there is a covenant upon the neck of his allies and his Shia, and among the completion of fulfilling the covenant and good performance is the visiting of their graves. So whoever visits them with desire for their visitation and affirmation of what they desired, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.وَفَاءٌ: Fulfillment or keeping of a promise

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting the graves of the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) defines grave visitation (Ziyarat) not merely as a ritual but as the fulfillment of a spiritual covenant ('Ahd') binding the Shia to their Imams. This act of sincere remembrance serves as a tangible proof of loyalty, securing the Imam's intercession (Shafa'ah) on the Day of Judgment, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology and the continuity of spiritual authority after the Prophet.
